title: ExamExtraction
description: What a model may propose after reading an uploaded exam document, and nothing more. This is a review proposal, not an exam: it becomes a ParsedExamCandidate that a staff member confirms. The envelope an exam needs to be sat - variant, timing, and raw-to-band scoring - is deliberately absent, because those are equated per exam version and attach to it as data rather than being readable off a page. Provenance is expressed as references to the source and chunk identifiers supplied in the request, so every proposal can be traced back to the bytes it came from and a reference the request never issued is a rejection.

contractVersion.description: Pinned so a stored proposal names the contract it was produced against. A new shape is a new value here, not a silent change of meaning.

title.description: A title proposal read off the paper. Null when the paper does not state one; never inferred from a file name.

classification.description: Unclassified and NeedsReview are first-class answers, not failures. A model that cannot tell which module a document belongs to must say so rather than guess, because a guess reaches a learner as a fact.

confidence.description: Metadata only, and nullable: no downstream decision reads it, and it can never move a band. A bounded number rather than a closed enumeration - the enum-not-range rule exists because a band is a decided value where 6.3 must be impossible, and this is not a band. Enumerating tenths would have rejected a legitimate 0.85 and invented a granularity no provider agreed to. The range is restated in the server mapper, because provider-side schema enforcement is a convenience this server assumes failed.

provenance.description: Where in the supplied sources this proposal came from. sourceId and chunkId are the opaque identifiers issued in the request; the server maps them back to archive entries. A reference the request did not issue is rejected rather than dropped.

answerKey.description: Copied from an official answer key printed in the source. Omitted entirely when the source carries none - an answer the model worked out itself is a guess even when it is right, and a well-formed wrong key marks every learner who sits the paper.

order.description: The number printed on the paper. Gaps are kept: renumbering to close one silently renames a question a reviewer is looking for.
